 My binge-worthy Korean dramas list includes Reborn Rich , Marry My Husband and Lovely Runner By Karishma Shetty October 26, 2026 When it comes to K-dramas, we love our traditional rom-coms and thrillers , but it becomes more enticing when there's a fantastical element to them. A sure-shot favourite is the time travelling trope, and Korean dramas like Song Joong Ki's Reborn Rich know how to do it right, as long as you're a willing “suspension of disbelief” participant.
 Now, as someone who has watched over 100 K-dramas, I reveal my favourite time travel K-dramas of all time. These handpicked selects seamlessly oscillate through the past, present and future, and feature intriguing stories with complex character arcs. Hint: They star Hallyu actors like Song Joong Ki, Park Min Young, Byeon Woo Seok and more…
 1. Mr. Queen
 At the top of my time travel binge list has to be Mr. Queen , THE K-drama that warmed me towards sageuks (historical dramas). Shifting from the 21st century to the Joseon Era, it's the main character body-and-soul swap between Choi Jin Hyuk's playboy chef and Shin Hye Sun's innocent queen that's truly witty to witness on-screen.
 2. Reborn Rich
 Another binge-worthy time travel K-drama in the recent past is Reborn Rich , which would give Bollywood movies like Om Shanti Om a “dramatic” run for its money. Song Joong Ki doing double duty as a betrayed secretary and a vengeful chaebol grandson will have you devouring episode after episode in one go, despite how unbelievable the “time” aspect gets.
 3. Twinkling Watermelon
 What sets Twinkling Watermelon apart from most time travel K-dramas is how rooted it is in one ordinary family. Ryeon's teenage CODA character travels back in time and gradually learns that his parents were once kids with dreams too. At the end of the day, it's all about loving your family, flaws and all, and sometimes it takes starting a band with your father (Choi Hyun Wook, Choi Wong Young) to truly embrace that feeling.
 4. Bon Appétit, Your Majesty
 The reason why the time travel trope is so loved is because of the hilarious interactions we are blessed with between characters from the past and present. Bon Appétit, Your Majesty is the best example, as YoonA's top chef of the modern era and Lee Chae Min's tyrant king and gourmet clash with hilarious outcomes. What eventually weaves them together is their shared love for food.
 5. Lovely Runner
 “Sunjaeyaaa…” is a phrase that's become synonymous with the Lovely Runner fandom, who will never ever get over the global hysteria created by this must-watch drama and its talented stars, Byeon Woo Seok and Kim Hye Yoon. Watching the heartwarming love story between a devoted fan and her idol as the former fights the laws of physics to save the latter from his doomed fate is as good as time travel gets.
 6. 18 Again
 18 Again shows us how the main character (Lee Do Hyun, Yoon Sang Hyun), through the medium of time travel, realise the true value of family. Whether it's his role as a devoted husband or a caring father, you simply can't take those relationships for granted, especially when the going gets tough. But it's not just an emotional roller coaster ride between the past and present, but also a hilarious one. Seeing the dad come back to his teenage self, only to go to school with his own kids, the shenanigans that ensue are worth watching!
 7. Marry My Husband
 Using time travel to take slow, steady, sweet revenge on your sh*thole of a husband (Lee Yi Kyung) and your best friend aka his mistress (Song Ha Yoon), while also getting your own second shot at happiness is Marry My Husband in a nutshell for you. Park Min Young's lead character transformation from the scorned woman to the woman in charge of her enemies' doom is delectable to watch unfold on the small screen.
 This article originally appeared on GQ India. 
 Karishma Shetty is an Entertainment Editor at GQ India where she covers entertainment and lifestyle, with special emphasis on celebrity, interviews, and movie & show recommendations.
